anya: quick note - JS SDK is silently dropping `max_batch_size` when callers use camelCase (e.g. `batchingHint`) -> REST expects `batching_hint` or `max_batch_size`. sample app throughput regressed after the frontend update. :confused:
sam: can you paste a tiny repro so I can poke?
anya: sure, super tiny. REST honors big batches; SDK falls back to default 8 instead of 64.
anya: ```bash
# REST (respects max_batch_size)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-xxl","batching_hint":0.9,"max_batch_size":64,"inputs":["a","b","c"]}'

# JS SDK (silently sends default max_batch_size)
import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ token: process.env.TOKEN });
await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-xxl', inputs: ['a','b','c'], batchingHint: 0.9, maxBatchSize: 64 });
```
qa-bot: quick log check: for request id `01GHIJKL5678` the payload normalized to `{max_batch_size:8}` on the wire.
anya: exact. also noticed an auth/retry quirk: our sample app retries on 401, but the control plane occasionally returns 403 during ephemeral-token refresh races. SDK treats 403 as non-retryable so the app retry triggers at the app layer and you can get duplicate side-effects (webhook deliveries).
sam: so two things: (1) param normalization across SDKs (camelCase vs snake_case) and (2) ambiguous retry semantics between 401 vs 403 for ephemeral flows.
anya: opened DEVEX-8002 with traces and minimal repro attached.
qa-bot: suggested mitigation: SDK should warn in dev-mode when unknown fields are dropped and offer a `strict: true` option to surface errors. also recommended adding an integration that compares SDK outgoing payload to a direct REST call to assert parity.
sam: plan: add aliasing shim in JS SDK to accept camelCase and map to `max_batch_size`/`batching_hint` with a console.warn in dev. add unit + integration tests to cover payload parity and 401/403 retry behavior in the sampleapp harness.
anya: please also update the sampleapp README with a note about retrying idempotent vs non-idempotent routes so customers avoid accidental duplicates.
devex-bot: Created task DEVEX-12456 from this thread and assigned to @sam.
sam: thanks, PR incoming. i'll also open an SDK-epic to consider generating input validators from the API spec to avoid name drift. :rocket:
